indication.text: Treatment of complicated intra-abdominal infections and complicated urinary tract infections, including pyelonephritis, caused by susceptible designated microorganisms

citations.quote:
- Complicated intra-abdominal infections (1.1)
- Complicated urinary tract infections, including pyelonephritis (1.2)

This new drug application provides for the use of DORIBAX™ (doripenem for injection) for the treatment of complicated intra-abdominal (cIAI)) and complicated urinary tract (cUTI) infections caused by susceptible isolates of the designated microorganisms.

target_moa.text: Carbapenem (beta-lactam) antibacterial; bactericidal via inhibition of bacterial cell wall biosynthesis by inactivating multiple penicillin-binding proteins (PBPs)

citations.quote: Doripenem belongs to the carbapenem class of antimicrobials. Doripenem exerts its bactericidal activity by inhibiting bacterial cell wall biosynthesis. Doripenem inactivates multiple essential penicillin-binding proteins (PBPs) resulting in inhibition of cell wall synthesis with subsequent cell death.
Doripenem is an injectable, synthetic, carbapenem in the \beta-lactam class of antibacterial agents.

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (≥5%) were headache, nausea, diarrhea, rash and phlebitis. In cUTI, headache occurred in 16% (vs levofloxacin 15%); in cIAI, nausea 12% (vs meropenem 9%), diarrhea 11% (vs 11%), anemia 10% (vs 5%). Serious hypersensitivity (anaphylactic) reactions and C. difficile-associated diarrhea were warnings.
